steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary React dependencies are imported for state management.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState, which are essential for building React components with state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the NotificationSystem component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named NotificationSystem that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: Define a function called NotificationSystem that returns JSX containing a single div.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the NotificationSystem component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The NotificationSystem component is defined and returns an empty div.
successCriteria: A functional component named NotificationSystem exists and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the NotificationSystem component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but make sure it's named exactly 'NotificationSystem' and returns a div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you defined a function named NotificationSystem that returns a div.

steps.title: Initialize notifications state
steps.instruction: Inside your NotificationSystem component, use useState to create a state variable named 'notifications' initialized as an empty array.
steps.hint: Call useState with an empty array [] as the initial value, and destructure the returned array into a variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state initialization
const [items, setItems] = useState([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'notifications' ready to store notification objects.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with [] as initial value, and the state variable is named 'notifications'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the notifications state with an empty array.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with an empty array [] and naming the variable 'notifications'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside the component, use useState to create a state variable named 'notifications' initialized as an empty array.

steps.title: Define addNotification handler
steps.instruction: Inside the NotificationSystem component, define a function called addNotification that takes message and type parameters and adds a new notification object to the state.
steps.hint: Create a function that receives message and type, then uses setNotifications to add a new object with id, message, type, and timestamp.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named addNotification is defined that creates new notification objects and updates the state array.
successCriteria: The addNotification function is defined with message and type parameters, creates a notification object with id, message, type, and timestamp, and updates the notifications state using setNotifications.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the addNotification handler that will add new notifications to the system.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function properly creates the notification object with all required properties and updates the state correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The addNotification function isn't defined correctly. Check that it takes message and type parameters and properly updates the notifications state.

steps.title: Define removeNotification handler
steps.instruction: Inside the NotificationSystem component, define a function called removeNotification that takes an id parameter and filters out the notification with that id from the notifications state.
steps.hint: Use the setNotifications function to update the state by filtering the current notifications array, keeping only notifications whose id does not match the provided id.
steps.expectedOutcome: A removeNotification function is defined that removes a notification by its id from the state.
successCriteria: The removeNotification function is defined, takes an id parameter, and uses setNotifications with a filter to remove the matching notification.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the removeNotification handler. This function will allow us to remove notifications by their unique id.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function takes an id parameter and uses setNotifications with a filter to remove notifications where the id matches.
steps.feedbackWrong: The removeNotification function isn't defined correctly. It should take an id parameter and filter the notifications state to remove the matching notification.

steps.title: Create the main container structure
steps.instruction: In your NotificationSystem component, return a div element with className 'notification-system' that contains an h1 element with the text 'Notification System'.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement (return null;) with a JSX structure. Start with a div that has the specified className, and place the h1 inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a structured JSX layout with a main container and a title heading.
successCriteria: The component returns a div with className 'notification-system' containing an h1 with the text 'Notification System'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the basic layout structure for the notification system.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have a div with className 'notification-system' and an h1 with exactly 'Notification System' inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The structure doesn't match. Check that you're returning a div with the correct className and an h1 with the specified text.

steps.title: Add notification controls section
steps.instruction: Inside the NotificationSystem component's return statement, add a <div> with className 'controls' that contains two buttons: one for adding success notifications and one for adding error notifications.
steps.hint: Create a div with className='controls' and place two button elements inside it. Give each button appropriate text like 'Add Success' and 'Add Error'.
steps.analogousExample: // Example: Adding a controls section
steps.expectedOutcome: A controls section with two buttons appears in the component's structure, ready to be wired to handlers in the next step.
successCriteria: A div with className 'controls' containing two button elements is added to the return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the notification controls section with two buttons.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some controls, but make sure you have a div with className 'controls' containing both success and error buttons.
steps.feedbackWrong: The controls section is missing or incomplete. Add a div with className 'controls' containing two buttons.

steps.title: Create notifications container
steps.instruction: Inside the NotificationSystem component's return statement, add a div element with className 'notifications-container' below the existing controls section.
steps.hint: Place the new div after the controls section but still inside the main notification-system container.
steps.expectedOutcome: The notifications container div is added to the component structure, ready to hold notification elements.
successCriteria: A div with className 'notifications-container' exists inside the notification-system container, placed after the controls section.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the container where notifications will be displayed.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a div element with the correct className.
steps.feedbackWrong: The notifications container wasn't added correctly. Check that you've placed a div with className 'notifications-container' in the right location.

steps.title: Map through notifications state
steps.instruction: Inside the notifications container, map through the notifications state array and return a div for each notification with appropriate className based on type.
steps.hint: Use the map method on the notifications array to create a div element for each notification. The className should be 'notification' plus the notification type (e.g., 'notification success').
steps.expectedOutcome: The notifications container will have a div for each notification in the state array, with a className that includes the notification type.
successCriteria: The notifications array is mapped to create div elements, each with a key prop and a className that combines 'notification' and the notification type.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully mapped through the notifications state to display each notification in the UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the map method on the notifications array and returning a div with a key prop and appropriate className.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your code. You need to map through the notifications array and return a div for each notification with a key prop and className based on its type.

steps.title: Display notification content
steps.instruction: Inside each notification div, add a span element to show the notification message and a small element to show the notification type.
steps.hint: Access the notification's message and type properties from the map callback parameter. Use JSX curly braces to display them.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: displaying item details in a list items.map(item => (
{item.name} {item.category}
))
steps.expectedOutcome: Each notification element will display its message and type when rendered.
successCriteria: Each notification div contains a span with the message and a small tag with the type.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the notification content display. Each notification now shows both its message and type.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added both the span for the message and the small tag for the type inside each notification div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The notification content isn't displaying correctly. Check that you've added both elements inside the map callback and are accessing the notification properties correctly.

steps.title: Add close button to notifications
steps.instruction: Inside each notification's div, add a button element with the text '×' and className 'close-btn'. Wire its onClick to call removeNotification with that notification's id.
steps.hint: Place the button inside the notification div, before or after the content. Use onClick={() => removeNotification(notification.id)}.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each notification will have a close button that, when clicked, removes that specific notification from the state.
successCriteria: A button with text '×' and className 'close-btn' is added inside each notification div, with onClick calling removeNotification using the notification's id.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a close button to each notification, making it easy for users to dismiss them individually.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but check: does it have the correct text '×', className 'close-btn', and onClick that calls removeNotification with the notification's id?
steps.feedbackWrong: The close button is missing or not correctly configured. Ensure each notification div contains a button with text '×', className 'close-btn', and an onClick handler that calls removeNotification with the notification's id.

steps.title: Add clear all notifications button
steps.instruction: Add a button with the text 'Clear All' and className 'clear-all-btn' inside the controls section of your component. Wire its onClick handler to set the notifications state to an empty array.
steps.hint: Place the button in the controls section, which is currently empty. Use setNotifications([]) to clear all notifications.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a clear button
<button className="clear-all-btn" onClick={() => setItems([])}>Clear All</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'Clear All' button appears in the controls section. Clicking it removes all notifications from the UI.
successCriteria: The button has text 'Clear All', className 'clear-all-btn', and onClick handler that sets notifications to [].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a button to clear all notifications at once.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it has the correct text, className, and onClick handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or doesn't have the required attributes. Check the instruction again.
